factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models gives no chance of snow through Oct 11, with overnight lows of 38-64°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The GFS shows no chance of flakes through Oct 8 (coldest night 38°F), and the higher-resolution NAM is rain only, coldest 50°F, through Oct 3. All three forecast systems agree.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: CPC expects a very strong El Niño. But State College's 10 strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, so the model makes no El Niño adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Sep. 30 has run 2.5°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks the AO averaged +0.95, the NAO +0.12 and the PNA -1.05: no strong push of cold into the East. These patterns' effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters

factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Oct. 8-14 (issued Sep. 30).

factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Oct. 13 00Z run) keeps snow chances under 1% through Oct. 23, with the highest, 0.1%, on Oct. 17 as Friday's rain departs. Overnight lows run 32-64°F; the coldest night, 32°F, comes into Oct. 18 under clear skies, too dry for flakes.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: All five models agree the weekend cold arrives as the rain leaves, with only small flickers. The GFS (Oct. 13 00Z run) keeps a little snow in Saturday's departing showers, peaking at a 1.6% chance of flakes on Oct. 17, coldest night 33°F on Oct. 18. The European (Oct. 13 00Z run) is nearly dry that weekend (0.4% Oct. 17, 0.8% Oct. 18) and saves its peak, 2.1%, for a dry, chilly Oct. 22 (coldest 35°F), so the two split on timing. The higher-resolution NAM is rain only through Oct. 15 (coldest 50°F), and LAMP's hourly guidance shows 0% in the next day (coldest 57°F). Blended, no day this week reaches 1%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C and a strong to very strong El Niño is likely through the winter (CPC, Oct. 8). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 12 has run 2.5°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks the AO averaged +0.78, the NAO +0.35 and the PNA +0.11: positive AO and NAO tend to keep the coldest air bottled up north, so no strong push of cold into the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 13, 3:17 AM): near-record warmth today (highs near 80°F), widespread rain Thursday night into Friday with gusts to 40 mph, then a "windy and wet end to the week with first flakes" over the higher elevations only. Lake-effect rain and possibly snow showers are expected later Friday into early Saturday on the northwest mountains, with a minor accumulation (under half an inch) possible on the highest ridgetops. Snow is mentioned for higher elevations only (Oct. 16-17); frost and freeze follow, with Sunday morning the coldest. State College sits in the valley, so that adds no direct chance here.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Oct. 15-19 (issued Oct. 12). The nearest hazards are high winds Oct. 16 over the Upper Great Lakes and Oct. 17 over northern New England. Neither changes anything, because the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Oct. 18-22 and Oct. 20-26, both with 3/5 confidence (issued Oct. 12), under strong ridging over the East. Oct. 18-22 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Oct. 24-26, just past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below-normal precipitation Oct. 18-22 and near normal Oct. 23-26, both with 3/5 confidence (issued Oct. 12). The dry days fall inside the blend's range, where the models already set the chance; the near-normal stretch after changes nothing.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Oct. 20-26 (issued Oct. 12); CPC discontinued its risk of much below-normal temperatures and expects unseasonable warmth across much of the East in week 2. The Oct. 18-19 cold risk from earlier issues is dropped: WPC's newer outlook covers those days, and CPC's 6-10 day outlook has Pennsylvania above normal.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Oct. 24-Nov. 6)
factors.text: Equal chances for temperature from the Ohio Valley to New England (issued Oct. 9), so the history-based curve carries late October and early November. It leans dry toward the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast, which isn't counted at that range.

headline: Near-record 80°F warmth today gives way to a frosty Sunday morning, with first flakes only on the northwest mountains (Oct. 16-17). CPC keeps Pennsylvania warm Oct. 18-26, so the chance of October flakes is 31%.

The European (Oct. 27 12Z run) gives 0% every day through Nov. 5, stays dry until Nov. 3, then brings a soaking in the upper 50s to low 60s Nov. 3-5; its coldest reading is 41°F early Saturday. The NAM (Oct. 27 12Z run) has only light rain chances, coldest 43°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Oct. 27 20Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 43°F.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027 (CPC, Oct. 8). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 26 has run 2.5°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 13-26) the AO averaged +1.56, the NAO +0.47 and the PNA +0.05. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and the PNA has run negative for the past week, which favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 27, 1:09 PM): "Rain-free and mild conditions will persist through the end of October," running 5-15 degrees above average through the weekend, before "November will start off with a couple chances for rain." The point forecast (1:32 PM) has lows of 38-51°F, coldest Friday night, highs near 70 Thursday-Friday, and showers Sunday night into Monday (40-50%). No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 2-6 and Nov. 4-10 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 27), favored along the Eastern Seaboard and the Appalachians. The wetter lean nudges up Nov. 7-10, past the blend, though the warmth means most of it falls as rain.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Oct. 29 00Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% through Nov. 3, with only faint flickers of 0.6% Nov. 4 and 1.0% Nov. 5 in mild, showery air, then 0% Nov. 6-7, the last full day it covers. Rain chances stay at 5% or less through Nov. 1, run 11-27% Nov. 2-4, then peak at 37-55% Nov. 5-6. Overnight lows run 36-53°F, coldest early Saturday (Oct. 31), with 35°F by early Nov. 8 behind the front.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree: nothing wintry through the first week of November. The GFS (Oct. 29 00Z run) peaks at 0.1% Nov. 1-2, with a coldest night of 38°F early Nov. 1. The European (Oct. 29 00Z run) gives 0% every day through Nov. 6; it stays dry until a soaking rain Nov. 6-7, with a coldest reading of 39°F early Saturday. The NAM (Oct. 29 00Z run) has only light rain chances, coldest 39°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Oct. 29 08Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 44°F.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027 (CPC, Oct. 8). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 28 has run 2.6°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 15-28) the AO averaged +1.47, the NAO +0.42 and the PNA -0.08. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and the PNA has run negative lately, which favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 28, 9:23 PM): highs today could challenge daily records, 10-20 degrees above average, and the dry spell should last through Halloween and probably the first few days of November, with wildfire-spread concerns Friday and Saturday. Forecasters still see a modest signal for a frontal heavy rain and wind event around Nov. 5-7. The point forecast (4:32 AM) has lows of 34-53°F, coldest Friday night, and highs in the 60s to low 70s. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Oct. 31-Nov. 4 (issued Oct. 28). WPC's hazards for that stretch are heavy rain along the Gulf Coast and in the Southwest, heavy precipitation in the southern Rockies and southern Alaska, and high winds in Alaska and the High Plains; the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 3-7 and Nov. 5-11 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 28), with above-normal odds topping 70% from the Mid-Atlantic to the Great Lakes ahead of a trough. Nov. 3-7 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 8-11, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 3-7 and Nov. 5-11 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 28), as a trough and strong low cross from the Plains to the East. The wetter lean nudges up Nov. 8-11, past the blend, though the warmth means most of it falls as rain.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing cold or snowy flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 5-11 (issued Oct. 28). CPC flags a slight risk of heavy precipitation for most of the East Coast states and a slight risk of high winds for the Lower Great Lakes, Ohio Valley, central and northern Appalachians, Northeast and Upper Mid-Atlantic, both Nov. 5: rain and wind, not cold. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 7-20)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across Alaska and most of the Lower 48, including Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 23; next issue Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 12-20, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: Today could challenge record highs in the low 70s before a dry cold front brings a 34°F Friday night and fire-weather worries. The median holds at Nov. 17.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Oct. 29 12Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 7, with only a 0.8% flicker on Nov. 8 as colder air arrives behind next week's rain; Nov. 8 is the last full day it covers. Rain chances stay at 3% or less through Nov. 2, run 12-17% Nov. 3-4, peak at 34-51% Nov. 5-6, then ease to 18-35% Nov. 7-8. Overnight lows run 37-54°F, coldest early Saturday (Oct. 31), with 33°F by early Nov. 9.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree on a dry, mild first week of November. The GFS (Oct. 29 12Z run) peaks at 0.1% Nov. 1-2, with a coldest night of 39°F early Saturday and Sunday. The European (Oct. 29 12Z run) is dry until a soaking rain Nov. 5-6, then drops to 32°F early Nov. 8; that cold, dry night gives it a 6% peak on Nov. 7, though it shows no snow falling. The NAM (Oct. 29 12Z run) has only light rain chances, coldest 41°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Oct. 29 20Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 40°F.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027 (CPC, Oct. 8). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 28 has run 2.6°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 15-28) the AO averaged +1.47, the NAO +0.42 and the PNA -0.08. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and the PNA has run negative lately, which favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 29, 2:12 PM): a cold front sweeps through dry overnight, bringing gusts of 20-30 mph and an elevated risk of wildfire spread Friday afternoon; the dry, mild spell lasts through Halloween and the first few days of November, with a building signal for an appreciable rain and possible wind event in the second half of next week. The point forecast (4:32 PM) has lows of 34-54°F, coldest Friday night, and highs in the 60s. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 1-5 (issued Oct. 29). WPC's hazards for that stretch are heavy rain in the Southwest Nov. 1, the lower Mississippi Valley Nov. 3 and the Southeast Nov. 4, heavy precipitation in southern Alaska and the southern Rockies, and high winds in Alaska and the High Plains; the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 4-8 and Nov. 6-12 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 29). Above-normal odds top 70% from the Mid-Atlantic to the Great Lakes in the first period, but fall below 40% across much of the East in the second, as East Coast troughing may return late in the period. Nov. 4-8 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 9-12, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 4-8 as a trough and strong low move east from the Mississippi Valley, then near normal Nov. 9-12 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 29). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing cold or snowy flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 6-12 (issued Oct. 29). CPC flags a slight risk of heavy precipitation for much of the Central and Northern Appalachians, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Nov. 6: rain, not cold. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 7-20)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across Alaska and most of the Lower 48, including Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 23; next issue Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 13-20, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: A dry front brings a breezy, fire-prone Friday, and the European shows a near-freezing Nov. 8 after next week's rain. The 80% range opens a day later, on Nov. 11.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Oct. 30 00Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 8, the last full day it covers. Rain chances stay at 4% or less through Nov. 2, run 8-13% Nov. 3-4, peak at 29-56% Nov. 5-7, then ease to 7-16% Nov. 8. Overnight lows run 36-52°F, coldest early Saturday (Oct. 31) at 36°F, with 35°F by early Nov. 9.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree on a dry, mild first week of November with no snow. The GFS (Oct. 30 00Z run) peaks at 0.1% Nov. 1-2, with a coldest night of 38°F early Saturday and Sunday. The European (Oct. 30 00Z run) is dry until a soaking rain Nov. 5-6, gives 0% every day, and bottoms out at 38°F early Saturday; behind the rain it holds lows in the low 40s through Nov. 8. The NAM (Oct. 30 00Z run) has rain only, coldest 40°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Oct. 30 08Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 39°F.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027 (CPC, Oct. 8). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 29 has run 2.7°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 16-29) the AO averaged +1.37, the NAO +0.38 and the PNA -0.16. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 30, 4:15 AM): a dry cold front finishes clearing the state this morning, with gusts of 20-30 mph, low humidity and an elevated risk of wildfire spread this afternoon after almost two weeks without measurable rain. High pressure keeps early November dry and mild, and the next rain may hold off a day longer than expected, with chances of 30-50% Wednesday (Nov. 4) and 60% Thursday (Nov. 5). The point forecast (4:32 AM) has lows of 34-52°F, coldest tonight, and highs in the 60s. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 1-5 (issued Oct. 29). WPC's hazards for that stretch are heavy rain in the Southwest Nov. 1, the lower Mississippi Valley Nov. 3 and the Southeast Nov. 4, heavy precipitation in southern Alaska and the southern Rockies, and high winds in Alaska and the High Plains; the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 4-8 and Nov. 6-12 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 29). Above-normal odds top 70% from the Mid-Atlantic to the Great Lakes in the first period, but fall below 40% across much of the East in the second, as East Coast troughing may return late in the period. Nov. 4-8 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 9-12, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 4-8 as a trough and strong low move east from the Mississippi Valley, then near normal Nov. 9-12 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 29). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing cold or snowy flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 6-12 (issued Oct. 29). CPC flags a slight risk of heavy precipitation for much of the Central and Northern Appalachians, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Nov. 6: rain, not cold. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 7-20)

The European (Oct. 30 12Z run) also gives 0% every day, stays dry until a soaking rain on Nov. 5, and bottoms out at 38°F early Saturday; behind the rain it gets down to 41°F by early Nov. 9. The NAM (Oct. 30 12Z run) has rain only, coldest 36°F early Sunday, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Oct. 30 20Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 40°F.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), with weekly readings near +2.5°C, and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 29 has run 2.7°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 16-29) the AO averaged +1.37, the NAO +0.38 and the PNA -0.16. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 30, 2:10 PM): the long run of dry, mild weather continues into early November, with a pleasant Halloween weekend and valley fog some mornings. An upper trough crossing the country reaches the East late next week, pulling Gulf moisture north along a front; rain odds are highest around Thursday (Nov. 5), and moderate to heavy rain is possible. The point forecast (4:32 PM) has lows of 34-55°F, coldest tonight, and highs of 61-68°F. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 2-6 (issued Oct. 30). WPC's hazards for that stretch are heavy rain and severe storms in the Plains Nov. 2, heavy rain in the lower Mississippi Valley Nov. 3 and the Southeast Nov. 4, heavy precipitation in southern Alaska, and high winds in Alaska; the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 5-9 and Nov. 7-13 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 30). A trough slides off the East Coast early in the period, with high pressure building behind it in week 2, and neither outlook calls for cold air in the Northeast. Nov. 5-9 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 10-13, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 5-9 as the trough brings rain to the Northeast, Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic, then near normal Nov. 7-13, with slightly drier odds in the interior East as high pressure builds (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 30). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 7-13 (issued Oct. 30). CPC's only hazards are heavy precipitation, high winds and mountain snow along the West Coast. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across the northern tier of the country under ridging over the Great Lakes, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 14-27, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: Still no snow in sight: dry, mild days give way to a soaking rain around Nov. 5, and CPC's week 3-4 outlook leans warm through Nov. 27. The late end of the 80% range slides two days to Nov. 27.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Oct. 31 00Z run, the newest available) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 9, the last full day it covers. Rain chances stay at 8% or less through Nov. 4, climb to 39-62% from the evening of Nov. 4 through Nov. 6, then ease to 12-30% Nov. 7-10. Overnight lows run 36-57°F, coldest early Sunday (Nov. 1) at 36°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree: no snow through the first week of November. The GFS (Oct. 31 12Z run) gives 0% every day through Nov. 7, with a coldest night of 35°F early Sunday (Nov. 1). The NAM (Oct. 31 12Z run) has rain only, coldest 39°F early Sunday, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Oct. 31 20Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 37°F. The European run isn't available today.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), with weekly readings near +2.5°C, and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 30 has run 2.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 17-30) the AO averaged +1.35, the NAO +0.39 and the PNA -0.23. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Oct. 31, 2:56 PM): ridging keeps it dry and mild through midweek, with highs 10-15 degrees above normal. Widespread rain returns Thursday and Friday as a complex system develops over the middle of the country; its details are still uncertain, but confidence is growing that the dry streak ends. The point forecast (4:32 PM) has lows of 35-57°F, coldest tonight, and highs of 63-70°F. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: The Oct. 31 issue was not available. The newest one on hand (issued Oct. 30) flagged nothing near Pennsylvania for Nov. 2-6, and the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 5-9 and Nov. 7-13 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 30; the Oct. 31 issue was not available). A trough slides off the East Coast early in the period, with high pressure building behind it in week 2, and neither outlook calls for cold air in the Northeast. Nov. 5-9 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 10-13, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 5-9 as the trough brings rain to the Northeast, Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic, then near normal Nov. 7-13, with slightly drier odds in the interior East as high pressure builds (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 30; the Oct. 31 issue was not available). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 8-14 (issued Oct. 31). CPC's hazards are all in the West: heavy precipitation and high winds along the Pacific coast and heavy snow in the Cascades, Klamath and northern Sierra Nevada, under a strong, long-lived North Pacific low. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 1 00Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 10, the last full day it covers (0.2% at most, Nov. 10). Rain chances stay at 12% or less through Wednesday, climb to 47-58% from Thursday morning through Friday, then run 16-39% Nov. 7-11. Overnight lows run 39-57°F, coldest early Nov. 10 at 39°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree: no real snow chance through the first week of November. The GFS (Nov. 1 00Z run) is the only one with any, 3% on Nov. 7 behind the cold front, with a coldest night of 39°F early Monday (Nov. 2). The NAM (Nov. 1 00Z run) has rain only, coldest 34°F this morning, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 1 09Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 35°F. The European run isn't available today.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), with weekly readings near +2.5°C, and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 31 has run 2.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 18-31) the AO averaged +1.31, the NAO +0.41 and the PNA -0.27. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 1, 3:08 AM): dry and mild through Wednesday, with highs 10-15 degrees above normal and lower 70s Wednesday. A cold front brings the first rain Wednesday night into Thursday, possibly only a 12-18 hour wet window, and cold air under a sharp trough could make the start of next weekend chilly and damp with a few showers. The point forecast (4:32 AM) has lows of 39-54°F and highs of 63-71°F. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: The Oct. 31 issue was not available. The newest one on hand (issued Oct. 30) flagged nothing near Pennsylvania for Nov. 2-6, and the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 5-9 and Nov. 7-13 (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 30; the Oct. 31 issue was not available). A trough slides off the East Coast early in the period, with high pressure building behind it in week 2, and neither outlook calls for cold air in the Northeast. Nov. 5-9 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 10-13, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 5-9 as the trough brings rain to the Northeast, Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic, then near normal Nov. 7-13, with slightly drier odds in the interior East as high pressure builds (3/5 confidence each, issued Oct. 30; the Oct. 31 issue was not available). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 8-14 (issued Oct. 31). CPC's hazards are all in the West: heavy precipitation and high winds along the Pacific coast and heavy snow in the Cascades, Klamath and northern Sierra Nevada, under a strong, long-lived North Pacific low. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across the northern tier of the country, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 14-27, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: October closed out without a flake, and the first week of November stays dry and mild until a cold front brings rain Wednesday night into Thursday. The median slips a day later to Nov. 19.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 1 12Z run) keeps the snow chance near 0% through Nov. 11, the last full day it covers (0.8% at most, Nov. 11). Rain chances stay at 10% or less through Wednesday, jump to 48-73% from Thursday morning into Friday, then run 5-37% Nov. 7-11. Overnight lows run 37-56°F, coldest early Nov. 11 at 37°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree: no real snow chance through the first ten days of November. The GFS (Nov. 1 12Z run) is the only one with any, peaking at 2% on Nov. 8 behind the cold front, with a coldest night of 39°F early Monday (Nov. 2). The NAM (Nov. 1 12Z run) has rain only, coldest 43°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 1 21Z run) gives under 1% for the next day, coldest 41°F. The European run isn't available today.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), with weekly readings near +2.5°C, and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Oct. 31 has run 2.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 18-31) the AO averaged +1.31, the NAO +0.41 and the PNA -0.27. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 1, 2:58 PM): dry and mild through late Wednesday, with lower-70s highs Wednesday. Showers start very late Wednesday or Wednesday night with a cold front, possibly only a 12-18 hour wet window, followed by slightly cooler weather and a chilly, damp start to next weekend. The point forecast (4:32 PM) has lows of 40-58°F and highs of 59-71°F. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 4-8 (issued Nov. 1). WPC's hazards for that stretch are heavy rain from the Ohio and Tennessee valleys into the southern Appalachians Nov. 4, heavy rain in eastern New England Nov. 6-7, and rain and high winds in southeast Alaska; the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 7-11 and Nov. 9-15 (3/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 1). Warmth is favored for the Northeast ahead of a southern-stream trough, then across most of the country in week 2. Nov. 7-11 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 12-15, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 7-11 along the Eastern Seaboard, then near normal Nov. 9-15, with the wettest odds staying near the coast (3/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 1). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: No cold flagged for Nov. 9-15 (issued Nov. 1). CPC posts a slight risk of heavy precipitation for the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Appalachians Nov. 9-11, with a possible nor'easter-like low along the coast, but that's rain, not cold, so it changes nothing. Its other hazards are heavy precipitation, mountain snow and high winds in the West. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across the northern tier of the country, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 16-27, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: CPC's newest outlooks keep Pennsylvania mild through Nov. 15, and the cold front's rain still looks brief, Wednesday night into Thursday. The early end of the 80% range slides a day later to Nov. 14.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 2 00Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 11, the last full day it covers (no more than 0.1% on Nov. 10-11). Rain chances stay at 14% or less through Wednesday, jump to 65-79% from Thursday morning into Friday, then run 10-36% Nov. 7-11. Overnight lows run 37-58°F, coldest early Nov. 11 at 37°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree: no real snow chance through the first ten days of November. The GFS (Nov. 2 00Z run) is the only one with any, peaking at 4.5% on Nov. 8 behind the cold front, with a coldest night of 38°F early that morning. The European (Nov. 2 00Z run) gives 0% every day through Nov. 10, brings close to an inch of rain Thursday, and bottoms out at 36°F early Nov. 8 and Nov. 10. The NAM (Nov. 2 00Z run) has rain only, coldest 46°F. LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 2 09Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 44°F.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), with weekly readings near +2.5°C, and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 1 has run 2.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 19-Nov. 1) the AO averaged +1.16, the NAO +0.39 and the PNA -0.25. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 2, 4:39 AM): mild and mostly dry through Wednesday, with highs 10-15 degrees above normal and lower 70s Wednesday. A cold front brings rain very late Wednesday or Wednesday night into Thursday, possibly only a 12-18 hour wet window, then it turns 8-15 degrees cooler, with a chilly, damp start to the weekend and a few showers. The point forecast (4:32 AM) has highs of 59-71°F and lows down to 39°F by Sunday morning. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 4-8 (issued Nov. 1). WPC's hazards for that stretch are heavy rain from the Ohio and Tennessee valleys into the southern Appalachians Nov. 4, heavy rain in eastern New England Nov. 6-7, and rain and high winds in southeast Alaska; the blend already covers those days.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 7-11 and Nov. 9-15 (3/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 1). Warmth is favored for the Northeast ahead of a southern-stream trough, then across most of the country in week 2. Nov. 7-11 sits inside the blend's range; the warm lean trims Nov. 12-15, past it.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Above-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 7-11 along the Eastern Seaboard, then near normal Nov. 9-15, with the wettest odds staying near the coast (3/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 1). The wet lean falls inside the blend's range and near normal changes nothing past it.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: No cold flagged for Nov. 9-15 (issued Nov. 1). CPC posts a slight risk of heavy precipitation for the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Appalachians Nov. 9-11, with a possible nor'easter-like low along the coast, but that's rain, not cold, so it changes nothing. Its other hazards are heavy precipitation, mountain snow and high winds in the West. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across the northern tier of the country, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 16-27, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: Still mild and dry until a quick rain Wednesday night into Thursday, then a cooler, mostly dry weekend, with only the GFS showing a sliver of a flake chance Nov. 8. The median holds at Nov. 19.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 2 00Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 11, the last full day it covers (0.1% at most on Nov. 10-11). Rain chances stay at 14% or less through Wednesday, jump to 65-79% from Thursday morning into Friday, then run 10-45% Nov. 7-11. Overnight lows run 37-58°F, coldest early Nov. 11.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The GFS (Nov. 2 12Z run) is the outlier: it pulls colder air in behind the weekend front, with a coldest night of 35°F early Nov. 8 and a flake chance of 6% on Nov. 8 and 11% on Nov. 9. The European (Nov. 2 12Z run) disagrees, giving 0% every day through Nov. 10 and 2% on Nov. 11, though it also bottoms out near 35°F. The NAM (Nov. 2 00Z run) has rain only, coldest 46°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 2 21Z run) gives 0.3% at most for the next day, coldest 46°F. Weighted together, Nov. 9 lands near 3%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 1 has run 2.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 19-Nov. 1) the AO averaged +1.16, the NAO +0.39 and the PNA -0.25. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, and a negative PNA favors mild air in the East. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 2, 1:45 PM): dry and unseasonably mild Tuesday and Wednesday, lower 70s Wednesday. Showers arrive very late Wednesday night and run through Thursday with a cold front, possibly followed by another front and round of rain Friday into Saturday, then cooler, mainly dry weather through Sunday. The point forecast (4:32 PM) has lows of 37°F Saturday night and 35°F Sunday night. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Not available today: WPC's Day 3-7 hazards file couldn't be read this evening. NWS mentions no snow and the blend covers Nov. 5-9 anyway, so it wouldn't change the odds unless it flagged heavy snow or much colder air over State College.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania near normal for temperature Nov. 8-12, then above normal Nov. 10-16 (4/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 2). A trough sits over the East in the 6-10 day period, with warmth favored across most of the country in week 2. The warm lean trims Nov. 13-16, past the blend.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 8-12, then near normal Nov. 10-16 (4/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 2), with the driest odds over the Great Lakes, Northeast and Ohio Valley. Flakes need something falling, so the dry lean trims Nov. 12, just past the blend.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: No cold flagged for Nov. 10-16 (issued Nov. 2). The only eastern hazard is a slight risk of high winds for the Appalachians, Ohio Valley, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast Nov. 10-11, which changes nothing; the earlier heavy-precipitation risk for the East was dropped. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across the northern tier of the country, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 17-27, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: The GFS turns colder behind this weekend's front and gives Nov. 9 a small flake chance, though the blend and the European stay at zero. The median edges a day later to Nov. 20.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 have a median of Oct. 25, trending about 2 days later per decade. That puts 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 3 00Z run) keeps the snow chance at 0% every day through Nov. 11 and gives 1% on Nov. 12, the last full day it covers. Rain chances jump to 70-75% Wednesday night into Thursday, then run 3-37% Nov. 6-12. Overnight lows run 35-59°F, coldest early Nov. 9 and Nov. 12.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models agree there's no snow this week, but split on when the chill arrives. The GFS (Nov. 3 00Z run) brings it in behind the weekend front, with a coldest night of 33°F early Nov. 8 and flake chances of 6% on Nov. 8 and 7.5% on Nov. 9. The European (Nov. 3 00Z run) holds off until Nov. 11, with 0% every day through Nov. 10, 4.8% on Nov. 11 and a coldest reading of 33°F early Nov. 12. The NAM (Nov. 3 00Z run) has rain only, coldest 50°F, and LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 3 09Z run) gives 0% for the next day, coldest 49°F. Weighted together, Nov. 9 lands near 2% and Nov. 11-12 near 1%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: Niño-3.4 is +2.1°C (CPC, Oct. 8), and a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027. State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 2 has run 2.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 20-Nov. 2) the AO averaged +0.92, the NAO +0.30 and the PNA -0.14, though the AO dipped below zero on Nov. 2 and the PNA turned positive. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole, while a negative AO and positive PNA tilt the East colder. Their effect on the coming weeks is already built into CPC's outlooks, and past Septembers' values didn't predict first-flake timing, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 3, 4:28 AM): unseasonably mild through Friday, 10-20 degrees above average. A band of rain crosses Wednesday night into Thursday morning, ending a 17-day dry spell, with possibly more rain in southeastern areas Thursday night into Friday. Cooler this weekend, with showers favored downwind of Lake Erie. The point forecast (4:32 AM) has lows of 40°F Saturday night and 38°F Sunday night. No snow or flurries are mentioned.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC (issued Nov. 2, valid Nov. 5-9) flags heavy rain on Nov. 6 from the Mid-Atlantic coast into southern New England, east of State College. Nothing is flagged over town, and rain doesn't bring flakes; the blend covers those days anyway, so no change.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania near normal for temperature Nov. 8-12, then above normal Nov. 10-16 (4/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 2). A trough sits over the East in the 6-10 day period, with warmth favored across most of the country in week 2. The warm lean trims Nov. 13-16, past the blend.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below-normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 8-12, then near normal Nov. 10-16 (4/5 confidence each, issued Nov. 2). Nov. 8-12 falls inside the blend's range, so the dry lean barely touches the forecast.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: No cold flagged for Nov. 10-16 (issued Nov. 2). The only eastern hazard is a slight risk of high winds for the Appalachians, Ohio Valley, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast Nov. 10-11, which changes nothing. No earlier cold risk to carry over.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Above-normal temperatures favored across the northern tier of the country, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Oct. 30). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 17-27, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

headline: A warm, soaking rain Wednesday night into Thursday ends a 17-day dry spell, with no air cold enough for flakes in sight. The early end of the 80% range slips a day to Nov. 14. And today we lay the NAM to rest; its final words for State College were rain, 50°F, as they so often were.

headline: The first real flake chance of the season is on the board for next Saturday, near 11% at its best. The median nudges a day earlier, to Nov. 20.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: Since 1991, State College's first flakes have landed around Oct. 25 at the median, with a trend of roughly 2 days later each decade. Adjusted for that trend, 2026 starts from Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 6 00Z run, the newest available) finds a snow chance for Nov. 14, peaking at 11% on Nov. 14. Lows range from 30 to 65°F, with the chilliest nights on Nov. 14.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models show only a small snow chance, and they largely agree on it. The GFS (Nov. 5 12Z run) peaks at a 9.7% chance of flakes on Nov. 12, with a coldest night of 33°F early Nov. 13. The European (Nov. 5 18Z run) peaks at 55% on Nov. 14, its coldest reading 29°F early Nov. 16. For the next day, LAMP (Nov. 6 02Z run) says 0%. Put together, the highest daily chance is about 11% on Nov. 14.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance) (CPC). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 4 has run 3.2°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: For Oct. 23-Nov. 5, the AO has averaged +0.53, the NAO +0.32 and the PNA +0.22. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole. The AO has dipped below zero the last two days. That influence is already baked into CPC's outlooks, and the pattern in past Septembers didn't predict first flakes, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: From NWS's Nov. 5, 9:39 PM discussion: 1) Unseasonably mild through Friday with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell now over. 2) Trending cooler this weekend with lake enhanced rain showers beneath upper level low. Point-forecast lows: 38°F Sunday night, 37°F Monday night, and 37°F Tuesday night. No flakes are mentioned in the forecast.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC flags nothing near Pennsylvania for Nov. 8-12 (issued Nov. 5). The blend covers those days anyway, so nothing changes.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania is near normal for temperature Nov. 11-15 (3/5 confidence) and above normal Nov. 13-19 (3/5), both issued Nov. 5. That warm tilt lowers the flake chance for Nov. 16-19, beyond the blend's reach.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 11-15 and Nov. 13-19 (1/5 and 3/5 confidence, issued Nov. 5). Flakes need something falling, so the dry lean trims Nov. 16-19 a bit more.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: No cold flagged for Nov. 12-18 (issued Nov. 5). Nothing to carry over from earlier outlooks.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)
factors.text: Pennsylvania sits no clear lean for temperature Nov. 14-27 (issued Oct. 30). It doesn't move the odds.

headline: A cold shot brings an 8% chance of flakes Nov. 12-14. The median slides a day later to Nov. 21.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: The 35-winter record (1991-2025) puts State College's median first flakes at Oct. 25, drifting about 2 days later per decade; that sets 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend (Nov. 6 12Z run) has just a sliver of snow chance, 2.3% at best (Nov. 13), out to Nov. 16. Lows land between 29 and 41°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models see only small snow chances, and they mostly agree. GFS guidance (Nov. 6 00Z run) tops out at 11% on Nov. 12 and bottoms out at 34°F on Nov. 13. European guidance (Nov. 6 06Z run) reaches 32% on Nov. 14 and bottoms out at 28°F. The RRFS (Nov. 6 06Z run) shows no snow chance, coldest 37°F. The 3-km HRRR (Nov. 6 06Z run) stays at 0%, coldest 36°F. LAMP (Nov. 6 13Z run) has 0.9% for the next day. Weighted together, the highest daily chance through Nov. 16 is about 8.1%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: CPC's ENSO status is El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). In State College, strong El Niño falls since 1957 ran about a day earlier than others, too small to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Over Sept. 1-Nov. 5, State College averaged 3.4°F warmer than normal. A warm fall has been only slightly tied to later flakes over 35 years (correlation +0.12), which is too weak to use, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over Oct. 23-Nov. 5, the AO averaged +0.53, the NAO +0.32 and the PNA +0.22. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole. The AO has dipped below zero the last two days. CPC's outlooks already include their effect on the next few weeks, and past Septembers' readings didn't predict first-flake timing, so nothing extra is added.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 6, 7:34 AM): unseasonably mild through today with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell now over. Trending cooler this weekend with lake enhanced rain showers beneath upper level low, mixing with some wet snow showers early Sat across the NW Mtns and Laurel Highlands. The forecast lows are 37°F tonight and 38°F Monday night. Snow is mentioned for the higher elevations only (Nov. 7), so it adds nothing for State College. Their snow call is light snow for the NW mountains and the Laurel Highlands, mainly above 2,100-2,600 ft, far higher than State College at about 1,200 ft.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 9-13 (issued Nov. 5). The blend already covers those days, so nothing changes.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania is near normal for temperature Nov. 11-15 (4/5 confidence) and above normal Nov. 13-19 (3/5), both issued Nov. 5. The warm lean lowers the chance on Nov. 17-19, past the blend.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Precipitation is favored below normal for Pennsylvania Nov. 11-15 and Nov. 13-19 (1/5 and 3/5 confidence, issued Nov. 5). A dry lean means less falling from the sky, which trims Nov. 17-19 a little more.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 14-27)

headline: Snow appears in the forecast for the first time, around next Friday, with a peak near 11%. Overall the median moves a day earlier, settling on Nov. 20.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: Since 1991, first flakes in State College have a median of Oct. 25 and arrive about 2 days later each decade, so 2026 starts from Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: In the National Blend (Nov. 7 00Z run), snow chances first appear Nov. 13 and top out at 6.7% on Nov. 13, the highest of the forecast. Overnight lows run 28-41°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models line up on a snow chance, with the National Blend, the GFS, and the European all showing it. GFS guidance (Nov. 6 12Z run) tops out at 23% on Nov. 13 and bottoms out at 31°F on Nov. 14. European guidance (Nov. 6 18Z run) reaches 16% on Nov. 16 and bottoms out at 28°F. The RRFS (Nov. 6 18Z run) shows no snow chance, coldest 38°F. The 3-km HRRR (Nov. 6 18Z run) stays at 0%, coldest 36°F. LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 7 00Z run) gives 3.3% through tomorrow, with a low near 40°F. Put together, the highest daily chance is about 11% on Nov. 13.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: CPC lists El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so there's no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Over Sept. 1-Nov. 5, State College averaged 3.4°F warmer than normal. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Across Oct. 24-Nov. 6, readings were +0.47 for the AO, +0.36 for the NAO and +0.32 for the PNA. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole while a positive PNA tilts the East colder. The AO has dipped below zero the last two days. That influence is already baked into CPC's outlooks, and the pattern in past Septembers didn't predict first flakes, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS forecasters (Nov. 6, 2:38 PM): trending seasonably cooler this weekend into next week with bulk of precipitation confined near and southeast of Lake Erie. Forecast lows run 37°F tonight, 36°F Monday night, and 35°F Tuesday night. Snow is mentioned only for the ridges (), which adds nothing for town.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: For Nov. 9-13 (issued Nov. 6), nothing is flagged over or near Pennsylvania. No change to the odds.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania is near normal for temperature Nov. 12-16 (4/5 confidence) and above normal Nov. 14-20 (3/5), both issued Nov. 6. That warm tilt lowers the flake chance for Nov. 17-20, beyond the blend's reach.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 12-16 and Nov. 14-20 (4/5 and 3/5 confidence, issued Nov. 6). Drier air trims Nov. 17-20 slightly, since there is less to fall.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: The hazards outlook (Nov. 6) marks a slight cold risk for Nov. 14-15 across portions of the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, Southeast, and along the Mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain, Pennsylvania included. It lifts the odds on those days.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: Above normal temperatures favored across much of the country, which takes in Pennsylvania (issued Nov. 6). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 21-Dec. 4, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

changes: Put together, the median lands a day earlier, at Nov. 20.
CPC's hazards outlook flags a cold risk for Pennsylvania.
The top day in the model consensus gained ground, going from 8.1% to 11% on Nov. 13.
The GFS's peak flake chance climbed from 11% to 23%.
The European's peak flake chance dropped from 32% to 16%.
CPC's week 3-4 outlook went from no clear lean to above normal.

headline: Flakes are back in the forecast for Nov. 13-14; the models agree, and the best day reaches 13%. The median stays put at Nov. 20.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: Across 35 winters (1991-2025), first flakes in State College have a median of Oct. 25 and are drifting about 2 days later per decade, which sets 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 7 00Z run) shows flakes becoming possible Nov. 13, with the best day Nov. 13 at 6.7%. Nighttime lows span 28-41°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: A rare consensus: the National Blend, the GFS, and the European all show flakes. The GFS (Nov. 7 00Z run) peaks at a 20% chance of flakes on Nov. 13, with a coldest night of 34°F early Nov. 14. At its best, the European (Nov. 7 00Z run) gives 25% on Nov. 13. The HRRR (Nov. 7 06Z run) shows no snow chance, coldest 37°F. Weighted together, the highest daily chance through Nov. 16 is about 13%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory; El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance) (CPC). Strong El Niño falls here since 1957 have averaged about a day earlier than other years, which isn't statistically significant, so there's no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: At State College, Sept. 1-Nov. 6 came in 3.6°F warmer than normal. A warm fall has been only slightly tied to later flakes over 35 years (correlation +0.12), which is too weak to use, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: For Oct. 24-Nov. 6, the AO has averaged +0.47, the NAO +0.36 and the PNA +0.32. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole while a positive PNA tilts the East colder. The AO has dipped below zero the last two days. CPC's outlooks already include their effect on the next few weeks, and past Septembers' readings didn't predict first-flake timing, so nothing extra is added.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 7, 5:07 AM): seasonably cooler this weekend into next week with bulk of precipitation confined near and southeast of Lake Erie. Lows in the point forecast are 33°F this morning, 35°F Monday night, and 37°F Tuesday night. Snow is mentioned for the higher elevations only (Nov. 7, Nov. 11, and Nov. 12), so it adds nothing for State College. Their snow call is accumulating snow for the NW mountains, the Laurel Highlands, and the ridges.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC outlines no hazards near Pennsylvania for Nov. 10-14 (issued Nov. 6). The blend covers those days anyway, so nothing changes.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: CPC leans near normal for Nov. 12-16 (4/5) and above normal for Nov. 14-20 (3/5), issued Nov. 6. That warm tilt cuts the chance of flakes on Nov. 17-20.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Pennsylvania leans below normal on precipitation Nov. 12-16 and Nov. 14-20 (4/5 and 3/5 confidence, issued Nov. 6). Flakes need precipitation, so the dry lean takes a bit off Nov. 17-20.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: A slight cold risk touches portions of the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, Southeast, and along the Mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain Nov. 14-15 (issued Nov. 7); with Pennsylvania only on the edge, it counts at half strength.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: Above normal temperatures are favored across much of the country, Pennsylvania included (issued Nov. 6). It trims the flake chance for Nov. 21-Dec. 4, beyond the 8-14 day outlook, at a light 2/5 weight.

headline: The first flake threat of the season takes shape around Nov. 12-14, topping out near 25%. The median edges six days earlier to Nov. 14.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: The 35-year record has State College's first flakes at a median of Oct. 25, creeping later by about 2 days a decade. The trend-adjusted starting point for 2026 is Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 7 12Z run, the newest available) finds a snow chance for Nov. 12-13, peaking at 8.5% on Nov. 13. Nights bottom out between 27 and 41°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: Agreement is strong on a snow chance, with the National Blend, the GFS, and the European on board. The GFS (Nov. 7 12Z run) peaks at 36% on Nov. 14. The European (Nov. 7 12Z run) peaks at 59% on Nov. 13, with a coldest reading of 33°F early Nov. 14. The 3-km RRFS (Nov. 7 18Z run) stays at 0%, coldest 40°F. The 3-km HRRR (Nov. 7 18Z run) stays at 0%, coldest 40°F. LAMP (Nov. 7 21Z run) puts the next day's chance at under 0.5%, with a low of 42°F. Taken together, the models give no more than about 23% on any day through Nov. 17.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: CPC's ENSO status is El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). In State College, strong El Niño falls since 1957 ran about a day earlier than others, too small to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: State College ran 3.6°F warmer than normal over Sept. 1-Nov. 6. In 35 years of records, warm falls have shown only a weak link to later flakes (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so there's no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 25-Nov. 7) the AO averaged +0.44, the NAO +0.41 and the PNA +0.41. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole while a positive PNA tilts the East colder. That influence is already baked into CPC's outlooks, and the pattern in past Septembers didn't predict first flakes, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: From NWS's Nov. 7, 12:42 PM discussion: seasonably cooler this weekend into next week with bulk of precipitation confined near and southeast of Lake Erie. Point-forecast lows: 34°F Monday night and 36°F Tuesday night. Forecasters mention snow at State College Nov. 12, which counts directly in the odds.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC flags nothing near Pennsylvania for Nov. 10-14 (issued Nov. 7). Nothing here moves the odds.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania is near normal for temperature Nov. 13-17 (4/5 confidence) and above normal Nov. 15-21 (3/5), both issued Nov. 7. Warmer air favored then pulls the flake chance down on Nov. 18-21, beyond the blend's reach.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 13-17 and Nov. 15-21 (4/5 and 3/5 confidence, issued Nov. 7). Drier air trims Nov. 18-21 slightly, since there is less to fall.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: A slight cold risk for Nov. 15 (issued Nov. 7) sits near Pennsylvania in portions of the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, Southeast, and along the Mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain, so it counts at half strength.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: CPC favors above-normal temperatures for Pennsylvania Nov. 21-Dec. 4 (issued Nov. 6). The warm lean trims Nov. 22-Dec. 4, after the 8-14 day outlook ends (it carries a 2/5 weight).

changes: Put together, the median lands six days earlier, at Nov. 14.
The top day in the model consensus gained ground, going from 13% to 23% on Nov. 13.
The NWS forecast discussion moved from a snow mention for the higher elevations only to a snow mention for State College.
On The GFS, the top flake chance went from 20% to 36%.
On The European, the top flake chance went from 25% to 59%.
The RRFS is back in the mix.

headline: Flakes show up in the model blend for Thursday through Saturday, peaking near 18%. The median now sits a day later, at Nov. 15.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: Since 1991, first flakes in State College have a median of Oct. 25 and arrive about 2 days later each decade, so 2026 starts from Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 8 00Z run) shows flakes becoming possible Nov. 12-13, with the best day Nov. 13 at 20%. Rain chances peak at 69% on Nov. 12. Overnight lows run 27-42°F, coldest Nov. 14.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: Most of the models line up on a snow chance, led by the National Blend, the GFS, and the European. The GFS (Nov. 8 00Z run) gives 13% at most, on Nov. 14. The European (Nov. 8 00Z run) reaches 63% on Nov. 14 at best, and its lowest reading is 33°F. The HRRR (Nov. 8 06Z run) keeps flakes out of its forecast, coldest 39°F. Blended by weight, no day through Nov. 17 gets above about 18%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: CPC lists El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so there's no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 7 came in 3.7°F warmer than normal for State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: The AO, NAO and PNA averaged +0.44, +0.41 and +0.41 over Oct. 25-Nov. 7. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole while a positive PNA tilts the East colder. CPC's outlooks already include their effect on the coming weeks, and past Septembers' readings didn't predict first-flake timing, so there's no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS forecasters (Nov. 8, 4:53 AM) say: seasonably cool today into the upcoming week with the bulk of showers from the next, fast-moving upper level disturbance confined to the Northern Mountains of PA late tonight and Monday morning. Lows in the point forecast are 35°F tomorrow night, 36°F Tuesday night, and 37°F Wednesday night. Snow is mentioned for State College Nov. 12, so the forecast chance goes directly into the model.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: For Nov. 11-15 (issued Nov. 7), nothing is flagged over or near Pennsylvania. No change to the odds.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: CPC leans near normal for Nov. 13-17 (4/5) and above normal for Nov. 15-21 (3/5), issued Nov. 7. The warm lean trims the chance on Nov. 18-21, past the blend.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: CPC favors below normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 13-17 and Nov. 15-21 (4/5 and 3/5 confidence, issued Nov. 7). Flakes need precipitation, so the dry lean takes a bit off Nov. 18-21.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: A slight cold risk touches portions of the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, Southeast, and along the Mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain Nov. 15 (issued Nov. 8); with Pennsylvania only on the edge, it counts at half strength.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: Above normal temperatures are favored across much of the country, Pennsylvania included (issued Nov. 6). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 22-Dec. 4, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

changes: The median moved a day later, to Nov. 15.
The best daily chance of flakes in the model consensus fell from 23% to 18%, now on Nov. 13.
The GFS trimmed its best flake day, from 36% to 13%.
On The European, the top flake chance went from 59% to 63%.
The RRFS dropped out of today's forecast.

headline: The National Blend, the GFS, and the European show flakes around Nov. 12-17; the best day sits near 25%. The curve's middle moves a day earlier, to Nov. 14.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: The 35-winter record (1991-2025) puts State College's median first flakes at Oct. 25, drifting about 2 days later per decade; that sets 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 8 12Z run, the newest available) finds a snow chance for Nov. 12-13, peaking at 21% on Nov. 13. Nov. 12 is the wet day, with a 72% chance of rain. Nights bottom out between 27 and 42°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: Agreement is strong on a snow chance, with the National Blend, the GFS, and the European on board. At its best, the GFS (Nov. 8 12Z run) gives 13% on Nov. 14. The European (Nov. 8 12Z run) gives 65% at best, on Nov. 13. The RRFS (Nov. 8 18Z run) keeps flakes out of its forecast, coldest 39°F. The 3-km HRRR (Nov. 8 18Z run) stays at 0%, coldest 37°F. LAMP's hourly guidance (Nov. 8 21Z run) gives 0.9% for the next day, coldest 45°F. Put together, the highest daily chance is about 23% on Nov. 13.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory (El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance), CPC). Strong El Niño falls here since 1957 ran about a day earlier than other years, which isn't significant, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 7 has run 3.7°F warmer than normal at State College. In the 35-year record, warm falls have been only slightly later (correlation +0.12), which is too weak to matter, so there's no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: For Oct. 26-Nov. 8, the AO has averaged +0.36, the NAO +0.43 and the PNA +0.56. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole while a positive PNA tilts the East colder. CPC's outlooks already include their effect on the next few weeks, and past Septembers' readings didn't predict first-flake timing, so nothing extra is added.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: NWS (Nov. 8, 1:56 PM): windy start to the week with light rain in the northern tier. First accumulating snow of the season possible for late week. The point forecast shows lows of 34°F tomorrow night, 35°F Tuesday night, and 37°F Wednesday night. The higher elevations get a snow mention (Nov. 8, Nov. 9, and Nov. 12), but State College doesn't, so nothing changes. The discussion has accumulating snow for the northern tier and the higher elevations.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC flags nothing near Pennsylvania for Nov. 11-15 (issued Nov. 8). That adds nothing to the odds.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania is near normal for temperature Nov. 14-18 (5/5 confidence) and above normal Nov. 16-22 (4/5), both issued Nov. 8. Warmth favored through then trims the chance on Nov. 19-22, past the blend.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: CPC favors below normal precipitation in Pennsylvania Nov. 14-18 and Nov. 16-22 (5/5 and 4/5 confidence, issued Nov. 8). A dry lean means less to fall, which trims Nov. 19-22 slightly.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing cold is flagged for Nov. 15-21 (issued Nov. 8); the only eastern hazard is a slight risk of heavy precipitation for portions of Southern California and the Desert Southwest Nov. 16-17 and a slight risk of heavy precipitation for portions of the Southern and Central Plains and the Lower and Middle Mississippi Valley Nov. 18-20, which doesn't change anything.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: CPC favors above-normal temperatures for Pennsylvania Nov. 21-Dec. 4 (issued Nov. 6). The warm lean takes a little off Nov. 23-Dec. 4, beyond the 8-14 day outlook, with a 2/5 weight.
