changes: All told, the median slid a day earlier to Nov. 14.
The best daily chance of flakes in the model consensus rose from 18% to 23%, now on Nov. 13.
The NWS forecast discussion moved from a snow mention for State College to a snow mention for the higher elevations only.
The RRFS is back in the mix.
In the 80% range, the early end moved a day later to Nov. 13.
The blend's last full day moved from Nov. 17 to Nov. 18.

headline: Snow appears in the forecast for the first time, around Nov. 13-16, with a peak near 12%. Overall, the median is six days later, at Nov. 20.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: The 35-year record has State College's first flakes at a median of Oct. 25, creeping later by about 2 days a decade. The trend-adjusted starting point for 2026 is Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: In the National Blend (Nov. 9 00Z run), snow chances first appear Nov. 13 and top out at 13% on Nov. 13, the highest of the forecast. Precipitation chances reach 81% on Nov. 12, but it falls as rain. Overnight lows run 29-39°F, with the coldest nights around Nov. 14.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: The models line up on a snow chance, with the National Blend, the GFS, and the European all showing it. The GFS (Nov. 9 00Z run) peaks at 15% on Nov. 14, with a low of 34°F on Nov. 14. The European (Nov. 9 00Z run) peaks at 26% on Nov. 16, its coldest reading 27°F early Nov. 19. The HRRR (Nov. 9 06Z run) shows no snow chance, coldest 38°F. Blended by weight, no day through Nov. 18 gets above about 12%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance) (CPC). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 8 came in 3.7°F warmer than normal for State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Across Oct. 26-Nov. 8, readings were +0.36 for the AO, +0.43 for the NAO and +0.56 for the PNA. A positive AO keeps the coldest air bottled up near the pole while a positive PNA tilts the East colder. CPC's outlooks already include their effect on the coming weeks, and past Septembers' readings didn't predict first-flake timing, so there's no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: In the Nov. 9, 1:22 AM NWS discussion: windy start to the week with light rain in the northern tier. First accumulating snow of the season possible for late week. Lows in the point forecast are 35°F tonight, 34°F tomorrow night, and 35°F Thursday night. Snow is mentioned only for the ridges (Nov. 9, Nov. 12, and Nov. 13), which adds nothing for town. Their snow call is accumulating snow for the northern tier and the higher elevations.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: Nothing flagged near Pennsylvania for Nov. 12-16 (issued Nov. 8). No change to the odds from this.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: CPC leans near normal for Nov. 14-18 (5/5) and above normal for Nov. 16-22 (4/5), issued Nov. 8. Warmer air favored then pulls the flake chance down on Nov. 19-22, beyond the blend's reach.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 14-18 and Nov. 16-22 (5/5 and 4/5 confidence, issued Nov. 8). Drier-than-normal weather trims the chance on Nov. 19-22, since flakes need precipitation.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: For Nov. 16-22 (issued Nov. 9), the outlook shows a slight risk of heavy precipitation for portions of Southern California and the Desert Southwest Nov. 16-17 and a slight risk of heavy precipitation for portions of the Southern and Central Plains and the Lower and Middle Mississippi Valley Nov. 18-20 in the east and no cold hazard, so nothing moves.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: Warmer than normal is favored for Pennsylvania across Nov. 21-Dec. 4 (issued Nov. 6). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 23-Dec. 4, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

changes: All told, the median slid six days later to Nov. 20.
The best daily chance of flakes in the model consensus fell from 23% to 12%, now on Nov. 13.
The European trimmed its best flake day, from 65% to 26%.
The RRFS is missing from today's runs.
In the 80% range, the late end moved two days later to Nov. 30.

headline: Flakes are in play for Friday, with the chance at 45%. The median slides six days earlier to Nov. 14.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: Across 35 winters (1991-2025), first flakes in State College have a median of Oct. 25 and are drifting about 2 days later per decade, which sets 2026's starting point at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: The National Blend of Models (Nov. 9 12Z run, the newest available) finds a snow chance for Nov. 13, peaking at 25% on Nov. 13. The best chance of precipitation is 86% on Nov. 12, falling as rain. Overnight lows run 29-41°F.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: Agreement is strong on a snow chance, with the National Blend, the GFS, and the European on board. The GFS (Nov. 9 12Z run) peaks at 31% on Nov. 14, with a low of 33°F on Nov. 14. European guidance (Nov. 9 12Z run) reaches 28% on Nov. 18 and bottoms out at 30°F. The RRFS (Nov. 9 18Z run) shows no snow chance, coldest 38°F. The HRRR (Nov. 9 18Z run) shows no snow chance, coldest 37°F. LAMP (Nov. 9 22Z run) has 0% for the next day. Weighted together, the highest daily chance through Nov. 19 is about 24%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance) (CPC). State College's strong El Niño falls since 1957 averaged about a day earlier than other years, not a significant difference, so no adjustment.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: At State College, Sept. 1-Nov. 8 came in 3.7°F warmer than normal. In 35 years of records, warm falls have shown only a weak link to later flakes (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so there's no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: The AO, NAO and PNA have averaged +0.22, +0.40 and +0.71 over the last two weeks (Oct. 27-Nov. 9). A positive PNA tilts the East colder. CPC's outlooks already include their effect on the coming weeks, and past Septembers' readings didn't predict first-flake timing, so there's no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: From NWS's Nov. 9, 2:24 PM discussion: tranquil weather expected with above-average temperatures expected through Wednesday evening. Potential for the first accumulating snowfall of the season, especially across the Laurels and the northern tier of Pennsylvania. Lows in the point forecast are 37°F tonight, 33°F tomorrow night, and 32°F Thursday night. Ridgetop snow shows up in the discussion; it doesn't count for State College.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC flags nothing near Pennsylvania for Nov. 12-16 (issued Nov. 9). The blend already covers those days, so nothing changes.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: Pennsylvania above normal for temperature Nov. 15-19 and Nov. 17-23 (5/5 and 4/5 confidence, issued Nov. 9). The warm lean trims the chance on Nov. 20-23, past the blend.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Below normal precipitation for Pennsylvania Nov. 15-19 and Nov. 17-23 (5/5 and 4/5 confidence, issued Nov. 9). Drier-than-normal weather trims the chance on Nov. 20-23, since flakes need precipitation.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: For Nov. 16-22 (issued Nov. 9), the outlook shows a slight risk of heavy precipitation for parts of Arizona, California, and southwestern Oregon Nov. 17-23 and a slight risk of heavy precipitation for eastern parts of the Southern and Central Plains, as well as the Lower and Middle Mississippi Valley Nov. 18-23 in the east and no cold hazard, so nothing moves.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: Pennsylvania leans above normal on temperature through Nov. 21-Dec. 4 (issued Nov. 6). That lowers the chance of first flakes Nov. 24-Dec. 4, past the 8-14 day outlook (2/5 weight at that range).

changes: The median moved six days earlier, to Nov. 14.
The top day in the model consensus gained ground, going from 12% to 24% on Nov. 13.
For Pennsylvania, CPC's 6-10 day temperature outlook switched its call, from near normal to above normal.
The GFS bumped up its best flake day, from 15% to 31%.
The European raised its peak flake chance from 26% to 28%.
The RRFS returned to the forecast.

headline: The odds of flakes on Friday have climbed to 30%, so the watch is on. The middle of the curve moves a day later to Nov. 15.

factors.name: 35 years of history
factors.text: State College's first flakes since 1991 center on Oct. 25 and trend about 2 days later per decade. Adjusted for the trend, 2026 begins at Oct. 29.

factors.name: Model blend, next 10 days
factors.text: In the National Blend (Nov. 10 00Z run), snow chances first appear Nov. 12 and top out at 27% on Nov. 13, the highest of the forecast. Rain chances peak at 82% on Nov. 12. Overnight lows run 29-41°F, with the coldest nights around Nov. 14.

factors.name: Model consensus
factors.text: A rare consensus: the National Blend, the GFS, and the European all show flakes. GFS guidance (Nov. 10 00Z run) reaches 18% on Nov. 14 at best, and bottoms out at 31°F on Nov. 14. The European (Nov. 9 18Z run) tops out at 78% on Nov. 13, with a coldest reading of 31°F. The RRFS (Nov. 10 06Z run) tops out at 4.4% on Nov. 12, coldest 32°F. The 3-km HRRR (Nov. 10 06Z run) stays at 0%, coldest 38°F. Blended together, Nov. 13 stands out at about 31%.

factors.name: El Niño
factors.text: Per CPC, El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). Strong El Niño falls in State College since 1957 averaged about a day earlier, too small to count, so the odds stay put.

factors.name: Fall warmth so far
factors.text: Sept. 1-Nov. 9 has run 3.8°F warmer than normal at State College. Warm falls have run only slightly later in the 35-year record (correlation +0.12), too weak to count, so no adjustment.

factors.name: AO / NAO / PNA
factors.text: Over the last two weeks (Oct. 27-Nov. 9) the AO averaged +0.22, the NAO +0.40 and the PNA +0.71. A positive PNA tilts the East colder. Their influence on the coming weeks is already in CPC's outlooks, and history shows no link to first flakes, so no extra adjustment.

factors.name: NWS forecasters
factors.text: The NWS discussion from Nov. 10, 3:16 AM reads: seasonable Warmup through Veterans Day. Late week rain and potential high elevation snow accumulation. The forecast lows are 37°F this morning, 34°F tonight, and 34°F Thursday night. The point forecast carries snow for the town (slight chance rain and snow on Friday and slight chance rain and snow on Saturday), so it counts directly.

factors.name: WPC hazards, days 3-7
factors.text: WPC outlines no hazards near Pennsylvania for Nov. 13-17 (issued Nov. 9). That adds nothing to the odds.

factors.name: CPC 6-10 / 8-14 day
factors.text: CPC leans near normal for Nov. 15-19 (5/5) and above normal for Nov. 17-23 (4/5), issued Nov. 9. That warm tilt cuts the chance of flakes on Nov. 20-23.

factors.name: CPC precipitation (6-10 / 8-14)
factors.text: Precipitation is favored below normal for Pennsylvania Nov. 15-19 and Nov. 17-23 (5/5 and 4/5 confidence, issued Nov. 9). A dry lean means less falling from the sky, which trims Nov. 20-23 a little more.

factors.name: CPC hazards, days 8-14
factors.text: Nothing cold is flagged for Nov. 17-23 (issued Nov. 10); the only eastern hazard is a slight risk of heavy precipitation for parts of Arizona, California, and southwestern Oregon Nov. 17-23 and a slight risk of heavy precipitation for eastern parts of the Southern and Central Plains, as well as the Lower and Middle Mississippi Valley Nov. 18-23, which doesn't change anything.

factors.name: CPC week 3-4 (Nov. 21-Dec. 4)
factors.text: Above normal temperatures are favored across much of the country, Pennsylvania included (issued Nov. 6). The warm lean trims Nov. 24-Dec. 4, after the 8-14 day outlook ends (it carries a 2/5 weight).
